questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India?
questions.explanation: Article 141 of the Constitution provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India. Article 142 relates to complete justice enforcement.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the oldest mountain range in India?
questions.explanation: The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world, formed during the Proterozoic eon, now deeply eroded into relict mountains.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune in 1905 to train national missionaries for the service of India and promote social advancement.

questions.question: Which one of the following metals is stored in kerosene oil to prevent it from reacting with atmospheric moisture and oxygen?
questions.explanation: Sodium and potassium are highly reactive alkali metals that react violently and exothermically with water and oxygen at room temperature, releasing combustible hydrogen. They are safely preserved immersed in kerosene.

questions.question: According to the Election Commission of India, in order to be recognized as a ‘National Party’, a political party must be treated as a recognized political party in how many States?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Solution: Assessed under Indian Polity & Constitution according to UPSC CDS standards.

questions.question: For which one of the following landmark judgments of the Supreme Court of India is the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) famous?

options.a: Evolution of the 'Basic Structure' doctrine of the Constitution
options.b: Right to Privacy declared a Fundamental Right
options.c: Formulation of the creamy layer principle in reservations
options.d: Striking down the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)

questions.explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), a 13-judge bench of the Supreme Court ruled by a 7:6 majority that Parliament has broad powers to amend the Constitution under Article 368, but cannot alter its 'Basic Structure'.

questions.question: In sociology and developmental psychology, which of the following is considered the primary and earliest agency of socialization for an infant?
questions.explanation: The family is the primary agency of socialization where a child first acquires language, behavioral norms, emotional attachments, and cultural values.

questions.question: The historic 'Panchsheel' (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was formally enunciated in 1954 in an agreement between India and which country?
questions.explanation: Panchsheel was signed on 29 April 1954 in Beijing in the preamble to the Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between Tibet Region of China and India by Premier Zhou Enlai and Prime Minister Nehru.

questions.question: What is a 'Concordat' in international diplomacy and legal history?

options.a: A formal treaty or convention between the Holy See (Vatican) and a sovereign State regulating church affairs
options.b: A multilateral military alliance between maritime nations
options.c: A commercial tariff protocol signed under GATT
options.d: An extradition treaty between Commonwealth countries

questions.explanation: A Concordat is an official bilateral convention or agreement concluded between the Pope (Holy See) and the secular government of a sovereign state.

questions.question: Which one among the following is the primary constitutional function of the Pro-Tem Speaker of the Lok Sabha?

options.a: Administer oath to newly elected members and conduct election of the Speaker
options.b: Preside over the joint sitting of Parliament in the absence of the Speaker
options.c: Check whether election certificates of all members are authentic
options.d: Decide on the disqualification of members under the Tenth Schedule

questions.explanation: The Pro-Tem Speaker is appointed by the President (typically the senior-most member) to preside over the initial sitting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha, administer oath/affirmation to new MPs, and conduct the election of the permanent Speaker.

questions.question: Which one among the following statements regarding the erstwhile Planning Commission of India is NOT correct?

options.a: It was established in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet
options.b: It was a statutory body established under an Act of the Parliament
options.c: The Prime Minister of India served as its ex-officio Chairman
options.d: It was replaced by the NITI Aayog on 1st January 2015

questions.explanation: The Planning Commission was neither a constitutional body nor a statutory body; it was an extra-constitutional body created by an executive resolution of the Government of India in March 1950.

questions.question: Which one of the following Fundamental Rights under the Constitution of India is also available to non-citizens (foreigners)?

options.b: Freedom to assemble peacefully without arms (Article 19)
options.c: Protection of life and personal liberty (Article 21)
options.d: Right to acquire and practice any profession (Article 19)

questions.explanation: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are available ONLY to Indian citizens. Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty) is guaranteed to all persons, both citizens and foreigners.

questions.question: Which one of the following is both a Fundamental Right under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution and recognized as a Universal Human Right?
questions.explanation: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A providing free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years. Free elementary education is also protected under Article 26 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

questions.question: With reference to the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Stock Exchanges and futures markets are listed under Entry 90 of the Union List (List I), not the State List. Forests was transferred from State List to Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

questions.question: Following the first schism in the Brahmo Samaj in 1866, who were the leaders of the two factions (Adi Brahmo Samaj and Brahmo Samaj of India) respectively?

options.a: Debendranath Tagore and Keshab Chandra Sen
options.b: Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Debendranath Tagore
options.c: Keshab Chandra Sen and Anand Mohan Bose
options.d: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar and Debendranath Tagore

questions.explanation: In 1866, the Brahmo Samaj split into the conservative 'Adi Brahmo Samaj' led by Debendranath Tagore and the reformist 'Brahmo Samaj of India' led by Keshab Chandra Sen.

questions.question: Under which operation codename did India conduct a series of five nuclear bomb test explosions at the Pokhran test range in May 1998?
questions.explanation: Pokhran-II, conducted on 11 and 13 May 1998 under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, was designated Operation Shakti. (Pokhran-I in 1974 was Operation Smiling Buddha).

questions.question: Which British Military Officer defeated Tipu Sultan in India, Napolean Bonaparte in Europe arid eventually became the Duke of Wellington ?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Indian History & Freedom Struggle).

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Gandhian mass movements is not correct?

options.a: Mahatma Gandhi was in favor of mass participation including peasants and women
options.b: Gandhian movements were rooted in the principle of non-violence (Ahimsa)
options.c: In Gandhian movements, disciplined organizational leadership played no significant role
options.d: Mahatma Gandhi advocated passive resistance and civil disobedience as moral weapons

questions.explanation: Statement (c) is incorrect. Centralized, disciplined leadership and strict moral command were vital hallmarks of all Gandhian campaigns (Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India).

questions.question: Which one among the following was the historic session of the Indian National Congress where the resolution for 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) was adopted?
questions.explanation: At the historic Lahore Session in December 1929, under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Indian National Congress adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution declaring complete independence as its ultimate goal.

questions.question: Which one of the following inscriptions mentions Pulakesin Il's military success against Harsh avardhana?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Geography (Physical, Indian & World)).

questions.question: Which one of the following traditional dance forms is a ritualistic folk dance involving masks made of arecanut spathe, performed in the temples of Central and Southern Kerala?
questions.explanation: Padayani (or Padeni) is an ancient ritualistic folk theater and mask dance performed in Bhadrakali temples of Central Travancore, Kerala.

questions.question: Who among the following Governors-General of India created the Public Works Department (PWD) and introduced electric telegraph and railways in India?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie (1848–1856) created the separate Public Works Department (PWD), introduced the first passenger railway (1853, Bombay to Thane), electric telegraph lines, and modern postal system.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ):
1. In the month of July, the ITCZ shifts northward over the Indo-Gangetic Plain (monsoon trough).
2. The ITCZ is a broad trough of low pressure characterized by convective clouds and heavy rainfall.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: The ITCZ moves northwards towards the Tropic of Cancer in boreal summer, positioning over northern India where it is referred to as the monsoon trough.

questions.question:
Which of the following National Parks of India are declared as World Heritage Sites by UNESCO?
1. Keoladeo National Park
2. Sundarbans National Park
3. Kaziranga National Park
4. Ranthambore National Park
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.explanation: Keoladeo National Park (1985), Kaziranga National Park (1985), and Sundarbans National Park (1987) are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Ranthambore National Park is not inscribed on the World Heritage List.

questions.question: Through which of the following states does the Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) NOT pass in India?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram. It does NOT pass through Odisha.

questions.question: What was the major international consequence of the Suez Crisis of 1956 following Egypt's nationalization of the canal?

options.a: Demonstration of the end of Great Britain and France as dominant imperial superpowers
options.b: Dissolution of the United Nations Security Council
options.c: Creation of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)
options.d: Direct military annexation of the Sinai Peninsula by France

questions.explanation: The Suez Crisis forced Britain and France to withdraw under US and UN pressure, accelerating global decolonization and highlighting their displacement by the US and USSR as premier superpowers.

questions.question: Which mountain hill range forms the natural physical boundary separating the state of Manipur from the state of Nagaland?
questions.explanation: The Barail Range is a tertiary mountain chain that extends across Assam, Nagaland, and Manipur, forming the water divide and physical boundary between Nagaland and Manipur.

questions.question: Which one among the following is the geological origin of the Comoros archipelago situated in the northern Mozambique Channel of the Indian Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Comoros islands are volcanic in origin, formed over an oceanic hot spot. Mount Karthala on Grande Comore is an active shield volcano.

questions.question: Which one of the following inland lakes in India has the highest water salinity?
questions.explanation: Sambhar Salt Lake in Rajasthan is India's largest inland salt lake and has the highest salinity among Indian inland lakes.

questions.question: Which one of the following trains/ railways passes through Germany, France, Austria, Hungary and Romania?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Geography (Physical, Indian & World)).

questions.question: Which one of the following ocean tides is produced when the Sun, the Moon, and the Earth are aligned in a straight line (syzygy)?
questions.explanation: Spring tides occur twice each month (during new moon and full moon) when gravitational pulls of the Sun and Moon reinforce each other in a straight line, producing the highest high tides.

questions.question: Which one of the following global climate types is characterized by mild, wet winters and warm, dry summers, supporting extensive citrus fruit orchards and vineyards?
questions.explanation: The Mediterranean climate (Cs in Köppen classification) features dry summers under subtropical high pressure and rainy winters dominated by mid-latitude westerlies, ideal for olives and grapes.

questions.question: A female Anopheles mosquito acts as the biological vector for which one of the following diseases?
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium parasites causing Malaria. Dengue, Chikungunya, and Yellow fever are transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.

questions.question: Down's syndrome, a genetic condition causing developmental and intellectual delays in humans, is caused by which chromosomal abnormality?
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome is caused by non-disjunction of chromosome 21 during meiosis, resulting in cells having 47 chromosomes instead of 46 (Trisomy 21).

questions.question: In demographic studies and development economics, the Dependency Ratio of a nation is mathematically defined as:

options.a: Ratio of dependent population (0-14 and 65+ years) to working-age population (15-64 years)
options.b: Ratio of unemployed persons to total employed workforce
options.c: Ratio of female population to male population in rural areas
options.d: Ratio of elderly population (60+ years) to total registered voters

questions.explanation: The dependency ratio measures the age-population ratio of typically dependent citizens (under 15 and over 64) relative to the productive working-age population.

questions.question: Lysosome is formed from which one of the following cell organelles?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing digestive enzymes that are packaged and budded off from the Golgi apparatus/bodies.

questions.question: The fundamental physical law which explains why a heavy steel ship floats on the ocean while a small iron needle sinks is:
questions.explanation: Archimedes' Principle states that a body immersed in a fluid is buoyed up by a force equal to the weight of fluid displaced. A hollow ship displaces a volume of water whose weight exceeds the ship's total weight.

questions.question: The natural plant dye Henna (Lawsone) imparts an orange-red stain to human skin and hair by reacting primarily with:
questions.explanation: The active colorant in henna is lawsone (hennotannic acid), which binds strongly through Michael addition to keratin proteins found in hair, nails, and the epidermis of the skin.

questions.question: What is 'heavy water' (D2O) used as in nuclear power reactors?
questions.explanation: Heavy water (deuterium oxide, D2O) contains deuterium atoms and is used primarily as a neutron moderator (slowing down fast neutrons) and as a coolant in Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs).

questions.question: What is the minimum mandate of a democratic government ?

options.a: Respond to ongoing priorities in public criticisin and threats to survival by decisive public action
options.b: Respond to demands of middle class pressure groups on an urgent basis
options.c: Preempt social agitations by enacting sensitive laws
options.d: Attend to severity threats that threaten national sovereignty

questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Defence, Military & Current Affairs).

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA) is not correct?

options.a: It empowers commissioned officers to fire upon or use force against persons acting in contravention of law in disturbed areas
options.b: It provides legal protection from prosecution without prior Central Government sanction
options.c: It can be applied automatically by local district magistrates without any disturbed area notification
options.d: The Central Government or Governor of a State can declare the whole or part of a state as a disturbed area

questions.explanation: AFSPA cannot be invoked arbitrarily by district magistrates; an area must be formally declared a 'disturbed area' by the Central Government, Governor, or UT Administrator under Section 3 of the Act.

questions.question: Which of the following chemical substances dissolves in water with a vigorous evolution of heat (strongly exothermic reaction)?
questions.explanation: Reaction of quicklime with water forms slaked lime [CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2] and releases large amounts of thermal energy (slaking of lime).

questions.question: Which one among the following was the nationwide anti-corruption citizen movement launched in 2011 advocating the enactment of the Jan Lokpal Bill?
questions.explanation: The 2011 Indian anti-corruption movement, organized primarily under the banner of India Against Corruption (IAC) and spearheaded by Anna Hazare, demanded an independent Lokpal.

questions.question: Which one of the following States of India is the largest producer of lignite coal?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Geography (Physical, Indian & World)).

questions.question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the topographical features of a river from its upper course to its lower course?
questions.explanation: Rapids form in the steep upper (youthful) course; meanders and ox-bow lakes form on the flat floodplains of the middle/lower course; estuaries or deltas form where the river meets the sea at its mouth.

questions.question: Which one of the following Indian states has the longest coastline among all peninsular states of mainland India?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest mainland coastline in India at approximately 1,600 km, followed by Andhra Pradesh (approx. 974 km).

questions.question: Which one of the following major rivers of India flows westward and empties into the Arabian Sea rather than the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapti rivers flow westward through tectonic rift valleys and empty into the Arabian Sea via the Gulf of Khambhat. Mahanadi, Godavari, and Cauvery flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: An object has a mass of 6 kg on the surface of the Earth. When taken to the Moon (where acceleration due to gravity is 1/6th that of Earth), its mass will be:
questions.explanation: Mass is an intrinsic property representing the amount of matter in a body and remains constant everywhere (6 kg). Only the weight (W = mg) decreases to 1/6th on the Moon.

questions.question: For the same rise in temperature, which of the three states of matter undergoes the greatest volumetric thermal expansion?
questions.explanation: Gases exhibit the highest coefficient of thermal expansion because intermolecular forces are minimal, allowing particles to move far apart when heated.

questions.question: In the human digestive system, the opening of the stomach into the small intestine (duodenum) is regulated by the:
questions.explanation: The pyloric sphincter is a band of smooth muscle at the junction between the pylorus of the stomach and the duodenum of the small intestine that controls the flow of chyme.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the United Nations based at The Hague, is composed of how many judges elected for a nine-year term?
questions.explanation: The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected by the UN General Assembly and Security Council for 9-year terms. Five judges are elected every three years.

questions.question: The human body's primary sensory organ responsible for maintaining balance, posture, and equilibrium is located in the:
questions.explanation: The vestibular apparatus in the inner ear, consisting of the three semicircular canals, utricle, and saccule, detects head motion and gravity to maintain balance and equilibrium.

questions.question: What is a 'Green Data Centre'?

options.a: A data centre created by environmentalists to keep records of clean production technology
options.b: A repository for storage and management of data where mechanical, electrical, and computer systems are optimized for maximum energy efficiency and minimal environmental footprint
options.c: A data centre for green buildings optimizing power consumption using solar energy
options.d: A repository providing information about small industries adopting energy efficiency measures

questions.explanation: A green data centre is an enterprise storage repository where lighting, electrical, cooling, and compute systems are engineered to achieve maximum power usage effectiveness (PUE) and minimal carbon emissions.

questions.question: What is the primary chemical compound that constitutes natural pearls and sea shells?
questions.explanation: Pearls and mollusk shells consist primarily of calcium carbonate (CaCO3, mostly in the form of aragonite crystals) deposited in concentric layers held together by the organic protein conchiolin.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements relating to the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) is/are correct?
1. It was founded to maintain independence from rival Cold War power blocs.
2. Military alliances formed a core component of NAM.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: NAM originated at the 1955 Bandung Conference and 1961 Belgrade Summit. Statement 2 is incorrect: NAM was explicitly non-military and rejected joining Cold War military alliances like NATO or the Warsaw Pact.

questions.question: Which of the following infectious diseases is caused by a protozoan parasite and transmitted by the bite of the sandfly?
questions.explanation: Kala-azar (Visceral leishmaniasis) is caused by the protozoan parasite Leishmania donovani and transmitted to humans by the bite of infected female phlebotomine sandflies.

questions.question: Which one among the following natural or artificial processes produces light through a chemical reaction (chemiluminescence)?
questions.explanation: Fireflies produce light through bioluminescence, a form of chemiluminescence where the pigment luciferin is oxidized in the presence of the enzyme luciferase and ATP without producing heat.

questions.question: Which one of the following elements is essential for the formation of chlorophyll in green plants?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Solution: Assessed under General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology) according to UPSC CDS standards.

questions.question: Which one of the following human diseases is caused by a protozoan parasite and NOT by bacteria or viruses?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium (transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito). Tetanus is bacterial; Measles and Mumps are viral diseases.

questions.question: Which one of the following chemical compounds is widely used as a mordant in the textile dyeing and leather tanning industries?
questions.explanation: Potash alum (potassium aluminum sulfate) acts as a mordant by providing aluminum ions that bind natural dyes to textile fibers, fixing colors permanently.

questions.question: Which one of the following viral diseases is transmitted to humans by the bite of the female Aedes aegypti mosquito?
questions.explanation: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes transmit Dengue, Chikungunya, Zika, and Yellow fever. Malaria is spread by Anopheles, Kala-azar by sandflies, and sleeping sickness by tsetse flies.

questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Defence, Military & Current Affairs).

questions.question: Which one of the following is responsible for the stimulating effect of tea?
questions.explanation: The stimulating effect of tea is primarily due to the purine alkaloid caffeine (also known as theine), which acts as a central nervous system stimulant.

questions.question: Fiscal Deficit in the Union Budget of India is defined as:

options.a: Total Expenditure minus Total Receipts (excluding borrowings)
options.c: Total Expenditure minus Tax Revenue only
options.d: Monetary deficit financed by RBI loans

questions.explanation: Fiscal Deficit = Total Budget Expenditure - Total Receipts excluding borrowings. It represents the total borrowing requirements of the government from all sources.

questions.question: Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), also known as 'paper gold', are supplementary foreign exchange reserve assets created by:
questions.explanation: SDRs were created by the IMF in 1969 to supplement member countries' official reserves. The SDR basket includes the US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi, Japanese Yen, and British Pound.

questions.question: The Phillips Curve in macroeconomic theory illustrates an inverse relationship between:

options.a: Rate of inflation and rate of unemployment
options.c: Tax rates and total tax revenue collection
options.d: Income level and demand for inferior goods

questions.explanation: The Phillips Curve, formulated by A.W. Phillips in 1958, shows an empirical inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.

questions.question: The difference between total revenue expenditure and total revenue receipts of the government in a financial year is called:
questions.explanation: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts. It signifies that the government is borrowing to finance its day-to-day administrative consumption expenditure.

questions.question: Which of the following macroeconomic policy measures is typically adopted by monetary and fiscal authorities to curb high inflation in an economy?

options.a: Raising the repo rate and reducing public expenditure
options.b: Lowering statutory reserve ratios (CRR and SLR)
options.d: Expanding public subsidies and tax holidays

questions.explanation: To tame inflation (contractionary policy), central banks hike interest rates (repo rate) to tighten liquidity and credit, while the government reduces public spending and fiscal deficits.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included while calculating the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of India?

options.a: Transfer payments (such as old-age pensions and scholarships)

questions.explanation: Transfer payments are unilateral payments made without any corresponding exchange of goods or services in return, and are therefore excluded from GDP calculations.

questions.question: Which one of the following public sector banks in India historically had an emblem featuring a dog with the motto 'Faithful, Friendly' before its merger with Canara Bank?
questions.explanation: Syndicate Bank, established in 1925 in Manipal, Karnataka, was famously known for its symbol of a faithful dog and the tagline 'Faithful, Friendly'. It was amalgamated into Canara Bank in 2020.

questions.question: According to the official Census of India, which one among the following Indian States has consistently recorded the highest female literacy rate?
questions.explanation: Kerala ranks highest in overall literacy and female literacy in India (over 92% female literacy).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Coast Guard (ICG):
1. It functions under the Ministry of Defence.
2. It is responsible for maritime search and rescue and marine environmental protection in India's EEZ.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) was established on 1 February 1977 and functions under the Ministry of Defence, mandated with safeguarding India's maritime zones, EEZ surveillance, and search and rescue.

questions.question: Under Article 368 of the Constitution of India, a Constitutional Amendment Bill can be introduced in:

options.d: Either House of Parliament or any State Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: A Constitutional Amendment Bill can be initiated in either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) and not in state legislatures. It does not require prior recommendation of the President.

questions.question: The historic Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and:
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 at Yerwada Central Jail between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, replacing separate electorates for depressed classes with reserved joint electorate seats.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is famously known as the 'Powerhouse of the Cell' due to ATP production?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP) through cellular respiration and oxidative phosphorylation, thereby serving as the powerhouse of eukaryotic cells. Lysosomes are suicide bags.

questions.question: The boundary line between India and China is known as:
questions.explanation: The McMahon Line was negotiated between Tibet and Great Britain at the 1914 Simla Convention, defining the boundary between Arunachal Pradesh (India) and Tibet/China.

questions.question: Who among the following Governors-General of India created the Public Works Department (PWD) and introduced electric telegraph and railways in India?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie (1848–1856) created the separate Public Works Department (PWD), introduced the first passenger railway (1853, Bombay to Thane), electric telegraph lines, and modern postal system.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ):
1. In the month of July, the ITCZ shifts northward over the Indo-Gangetic Plain (monsoon trough).
2. The ITCZ is a broad trough of low pressure characterized by convective clouds and heavy rainfall.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: The ITCZ moves northwards towards the Tropic of Cancer in boreal summer, positioning over northern India where it is referred to as the monsoon trough.

questions.question:
Which of the following National Parks of India are declared as World Heritage Sites by UNESCO?
1. Keoladeo National Park
2. Sundarbans National Park
3. Kaziranga National Park
4. Ranthambore National Park
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.explanation: Keoladeo National Park (1985), Kaziranga National Park (1985), and Sundarbans National Park (1987) are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Ranthambore National Park is not inscribed on the World Heritage List.

questions.question: Through which of the following states does the Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) NOT pass in India?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram. It does NOT pass through Odisha.

questions.question: What was the major international consequence of the Suez Crisis of 1956 following Egypt's nationalization of the canal?

options.a: Demonstration of the end of Great Britain and France as dominant imperial superpowers
options.b: Dissolution of the United Nations Security Council
options.c: Creation of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)
options.d: Direct military annexation of the Sinai Peninsula by France

questions.explanation: The Suez Crisis forced Britain and France to withdraw under US and UN pressure, accelerating global decolonization and highlighting their displacement by the US and USSR as premier superpowers.

questions.question: Which mountain hill range forms the natural physical boundary separating the state of Manipur from the state of Nagaland?
questions.explanation: The Barail Range is a tertiary mountain chain that extends across Assam, Nagaland, and Manipur, forming the water divide and physical boundary between Nagaland and Manipur.

questions.question: Which one among the following is the geological origin of the Comoros archipelago situated in the northern Mozambique Channel of the Indian Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Comoros islands are volcanic in origin, formed over an oceanic hot spot. Mount Karthala on Grande Comore is an active shield volcano.

questions.question: Which one of the following inland lakes in India has the highest water salinity?
questions.explanation: Sambhar Salt Lake in Rajasthan is India's largest inland salt lake and has the highest salinity among Indian inland lakes.

questions.question: Which one of the following trains/ railways passes through Germany, France, Austria, Hungary and Romania?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Geography (Physical, Indian & World)).

questions.question: Which one of the following ocean tides is produced when the Sun, the Moon, and the Earth are aligned in a straight line (syzygy)?
questions.explanation: Spring tides occur twice each month (during new moon and full moon) when gravitational pulls of the Sun and Moon reinforce each other in a straight line, producing the highest high tides.

questions.question: Which one of the following global climate types is characterized by mild, wet winters and warm, dry summers, supporting extensive citrus fruit orchards and vineyards?
questions.explanation: The Mediterranean climate (Cs in Köppen classification) features dry summers under subtropical high pressure and rainy winters dominated by mid-latitude westerlies, ideal for olives and grapes.

questions.question: A female Anopheles mosquito acts as the biological vector for which one of the following diseases?
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium parasites causing Malaria. Dengue, Chikungunya, and Yellow fever are transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.

questions.question: Down's syndrome, a genetic condition causing developmental and intellectual delays in humans, is caused by which chromosomal abnormality?
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome is caused by non-disjunction of chromosome 21 during meiosis, resulting in cells having 47 chromosomes instead of 46 (Trisomy 21).

questions.question: In demographic studies and development economics, the Dependency Ratio of a nation is mathematically defined as:

options.a: Ratio of dependent population (0-14 and 65+ years) to working-age population (15-64 years)
options.b: Ratio of unemployed persons to total employed workforce
options.c: Ratio of female population to male population in rural areas
options.d: Ratio of elderly population (60+ years) to total registered voters

questions.explanation: The dependency ratio measures the age-population ratio of typically dependent citizens (under 15 and over 64) relative to the productive working-age population.

questions.question: Lysosome is formed from which one of the following cell organelles?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing digestive enzymes that are packaged and budded off from the Golgi apparatus/bodies.

questions.question: The fundamental physical law which explains why a heavy steel ship floats on the ocean while a small iron needle sinks is:
questions.explanation: Archimedes' Principle states that a body immersed in a fluid is buoyed up by a force equal to the weight of fluid displaced. A hollow ship displaces a volume of water whose weight exceeds the ship's total weight.

questions.question: The natural plant dye Henna (Lawsone) imparts an orange-red stain to human skin and hair by reacting primarily with:
questions.explanation: The active colorant in henna is lawsone (hennotannic acid), which binds strongly through Michael addition to keratin proteins found in hair, nails, and the epidermis of the skin.

questions.question: What is 'heavy water' (D2O) used as in nuclear power reactors?
questions.explanation: Heavy water (deuterium oxide, D2O) contains deuterium atoms and is used primarily as a neutron moderator (slowing down fast neutrons) and as a coolant in Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs).

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA) is not correct?

options.a: It empowers commissioned officers to fire upon or use force against persons acting in contravention of law in disturbed areas
options.b: It provides legal protection from prosecution without prior Central Government sanction
options.c: It can be applied automatically by local district magistrates without any disturbed area notification
options.d: The Central Government or Governor of a State can declare the whole or part of a state as a disturbed area

questions.explanation: AFSPA cannot be invoked arbitrarily by district magistrates; an area must be formally declared a 'disturbed area' by the Central Government, Governor, or UT Administrator under Section 3 of the Act.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of international judicial or financial organizations and their headquarters is correctly matched?

questions.explanation: The ICJ is headquartered at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. IMF and World Bank are in Washington, D.C.; WTO is in Geneva.

questions.question: Which one among the following was developed as an indigenous high-performance supercomputer by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in 2011?
questions.explanation: SAGA-220 (Supercomputer for Aerospace with GPU Architecture-220 teraflops) was built by ISRO at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) using commercial off-the-shelf GPU hardware.

questions.question: Which one of the following synthetic chemical compounds is widely used by farmers as a selective systemic herbicide to destroy broadleaf weeds in cereal crops?
questions.explanation: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin herbicide that selectively eliminates dicotyledonous (broadleaf) weeds without harming monocotyledonous grasses (wheat, corn, rice).

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the commonly used automobile battery are true?
1. It is usually a lead-acid battery.
2. It has six cells with a potential of 2 Volt each.
3. Its cells work as Galvanic Cells while discharging power.
4. Its cells work as electrolytic cells while recharging.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.explanation: A standard 12V car battery consists of six 2V lead-acid cells connected in series. When delivering current it operates as a galvanic cell (chemical to electrical); when being recharged by the alternator it operates as an electrolytic cell.

questions.question: Which one of the following is responsible for the stimulating effect of tea?
questions.explanation: The stimulating effect of tea is primarily due to the purine alkaloid caffeine (also known as theine), which acts as a central nervous system stimulant.

questions.question: Primary Deficit in public finance is mathematically computed by deducting which one of the following from the Fiscal Deficit?
questions.explanation: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments. It indicates government borrowing requirements strictly to finance ongoing fiscal policies excluding past debt obligations.

questions.question: The Lorenz Curve in economics is a graphical representation used to measure:

options.a: Income inequality and wealth distribution in a population
options.c: Relationship between tax rate and tax revenue
options.d: Consumer price index variation over time

questions.explanation: The Lorenz Curve plots cumulative percentage of population against cumulative percentage of income earned. The Gini Coefficient is derived directly from the area between the line of equality and the Lorenz Curve.

questions.question: The concept of 'Gross National Happiness' (GNH) as a measure of national development progress was first introduced by which country?
questions.explanation: Gross National Happiness (GNH) was instituted in 1972 by Jigme Singye Wangchuck, the 4th King of Bhutan, measuring social development and environmental conservation alongside economics.

questions.question: What was the target deadline year set by the United Nations for achieving the eight Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) adopted in the year 2000?
questions.explanation: The Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) established eight anti-poverty and development goals with measurable targets to be achieved by the year 2015, succeeded by the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

questions.question: Which of the following rates is known as the key policy interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends short-term liquidity to commercial banks against government securities?
questions.explanation: The Repo Rate (Repurchase Option Rate) is the benchmark interest rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks against pledged government collateral.

questions.question: Which one of the following Indian states shares an international land border with three countries (Nepal, Bhutan, and China)?
questions.explanation: Sikkim shares international borders with three countries: Nepal to the west, China (Tibet Autonomous Region) to the north/northeast, and Bhutan to the east.

questions.question: According to the Election Commission of India, in order to be recognized as a ‘National Party’, a political party must be treated as a recognized political party in how many States?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Solution: Assessed under Indian Polity & Constitution according to UPSC CDS standards.

questions.question: For which one of the following landmark judgments of the Supreme Court of India is the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) famous?

options.a: Evolution of the 'Basic Structure' doctrine of the Constitution
options.b: Right to Privacy declared a Fundamental Right
options.c: Formulation of the creamy layer principle in reservations
options.d: Striking down the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)

questions.explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), a 13-judge bench of the Supreme Court ruled by a 7:6 majority that Parliament has broad powers to amend the Constitution under Article 368, but cannot alter its 'Basic Structure'.

questions.question: Which of the following authorities is vested with the power to alter the boundaries or name of any State in India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 3 of the Constitution, Parliament may by law form a new State or alter the area, boundaries or name of any State by a simple majority.

questions.question: Who among the following led the 1857 Revolt in Bihar?
questions.explanation: Veer Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur (Arrah, Bihar) led the 1857 Revolt in Bihar with exceptional guerrilla warfare tactics at the age of nearly 80.

questions.question: Which one of the following ocean currents is a cold current
questions.explanation: The Benguela Current is a cold ocean current flowing northward along the southwest coast of Africa in the South Atlantic Ocean. Gulf Stream and Brazil Current are warm Atlantic currents; Kuroshio is in the Pacific.

questions.question: The Western Naval Command of the Indian Navy is headquartered at:
questions.explanation: The Western Naval Command is headquartered in Mumbai (Maharashtra). The Eastern Naval Command is at Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), and the Southern Naval Command (Training) is at Kochi (Kerala).

questions.question: Which is the correct arrangement of the following peninsular rivers of India when arranged from North to South?
questions.explanation: From north to south: Mahanadi (Chhattisgarh/Odisha) -> Godavari (Maharashtra/AP) -> Krishna (Maharashtra/Karnataka/AP) -> Cauvery (Karnataka/Tamil Nadu).

questions.question: Which one among the following animal tissués transports hormones and heat and maintains water balance ?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Geography (Physical, Indian & World)).

questions.question: Which one among the following is the purest natural source of fresh water in the earth's hydrological cycle before touching ground pollutants?
questions.explanation: Rainwater is the purest form of natural water as it is produced by the natural evaporation-condensation cycle (distillation process) in the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which one of the following countries is located entirely south of the Equator?
questions.explanation: Australia lies entirely in the Southern Hemisphere, well south of the Equator (latitudes 10°S to 43°S). Colombia, Indonesia, and Kenya are all crossed directly by the Equator.

questions.question: Which one of the following glycopeptide antibiotics is commonly reserved in clinical practice as the 'drug of last resort' against severe multi-drug resistant Gram-positive infections (such as MRSA)?
questions.explanation: Vancomycin is a powerful glycopeptide antibiotic historically used as a drug of last resort for serious, life-threatening infections caused by Gram-positive bacteria unresponsive to other antibiotics.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a cold ocean current flowing equatorward along the southwestern coast of the African continent?
questions.explanation: The Benguela Current is a prominent cold eastern boundary current of the South Atlantic subtropical gyre flowing north along the coast of Namibia and South Africa.

questions.question: Which type of natural biome is characterized by low temperatures, short growing seasons, permafrost, and dominant vegetation consisting of mosses and lichens?
questions.explanation: The Tundra biome is treeless and circumpolar in high northern latitudes. Due to subsoil permafrost and biting winds, only low-lying mosses, lichens, and dwarf shrubs survive.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of the Indian Armed Forces:
1. The CDS functions as the permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.
2. The CDS acts as the principal military adviser to the Defence Minister on tri-service matters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: The CDS is a 4-star General who heads the Department of Military Affairs (DMA), chairs the Chiefs of Staff Committee, and acts as principal military adviser to the Raksha Mantri.

questions.question: If excess chemical fertilizer is applied to a potted plant without adding adequate water, the plant wilts and dies because of:
questions.explanation: High concentration of fertilizer salts creates a hypertonic external solution around the roots. Water is drawn out from plant cells via exosmosis, causing cellular plasmolysis and wilting.

questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Solution: Assessed under General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology) according to UPSC CDS standards.

questions.question: Wavelengths of which of the following colors of the visible light spectrum are maximally absorbed by chlorophyll in green plants for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a and b show maximum absorption in the blue (430-450 nm) and red (640-660 nm) regions of the visible spectrum, while reflecting green light (giving plants their green appearance).

questions.question: Which among the following are the two primary raw materials used in the saponification process to manufacture soap?

options.a: Fats/Vegetable oils and Caustic soda (Sodium hydroxide)

questions.explanation: Soap is produced by saponification, the alkaline hydrolysis of triglycerides (vegetable oils or animal fats) with a strong base such as sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) or potassium hydroxide.

questions.question: Which of the following noble gases is present in the highest abundance by volume in dry atmospheric air?
questions.explanation: Argon is the third most abundant gas in dry air (approx. 0.934% by volume). Other noble gases like Neon (0.0018%), Helium (0.0005%), and Krypton (0.0001%) are trace elements.

questions.question: Which of the following chemical compounds exhibits electrovalent (ionic) bonding rather than covalent bonding?
questions.explanation: Calcium chloride (CaCl2) is an ionic compound formed between a metal (calcium) and non-metal (chlorine) by complete transfer of electrons. CH4, CCl4, and NH3 are covalent compounds.

questions.question: Which one among the following substances is lipid-soluble and absorbed directly and rapidly across the epithelial lining of the human stomach into the bloodstream?
questions.explanation: Unlike most foods which require enzymatic digestion and are absorbed in the small intestine, ethanol is lipid-soluble and can be directly absorbed through the gastric mucosa of the stomach.

questions.question: Which one of the following places of India experiences highest atmospheric pressure during winter?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Solution: Assessed under General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology) according to UPSC CDS standards.

questions.question: Which one of the following is India's indigenously designed and built single-engine supersonic Light Combat Aircraft (LCA)?
questions.explanation: LCA Tejas is an indigenous single-engine, delta-wing multirole light fighter aircraft designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) and manufactured by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL).

questions.question: Which one of the following pairs of Indian military training academies and their locations is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: NDA is in Khadakwasla (Pune); IMA is in Dehradun; OTA is in Chennai/Gaya; INA is in Ezhimala (Kerala).

questions.question: Which one of the following alloys is commonly used for making heating elements in electrical appliances like heaters and electric irons?
questions.explanation: Nichrome (an alloy of 80% nickel and 20% chromium) has high electrical resistivity and a high melting point, and does not easily oxidize at high temperatures.

questions.question: Which one of the following physical properties decreases systematically as one moves from left to right across a period in the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period from left to right due to increased effective nuclear charge pulling valence electrons closer to the nucleus.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the commonly used automobile battery are true?
1. It is usually a lead-acid battery.
2. It has six cells with a potential of 2 Volt each.
3. Its cells work as Galvanic Cells while discharging power.
4. Its cells work as electrolytic cells while recharging.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.explanation: A standard 12V car battery consists of six 2V lead-acid cells connected in series. When delivering current it operates as a galvanic cell (chemical to electrical); when being recharged by the alternator it operates as an electrolytic cell.

questions.question: In which year did the Constituent Assembly of Nepal formally declare the country a Federal Democratic Republic, thereby ending the 240-year-old Shah monarchy?
questions.explanation: On 28 May 2008, the newly elected Constituent Assembly of Nepal voted overwhelmingly to abolish the monarchy and declare Nepal a Federal Democratic Republic.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 introduced Article 246A and Article 279A, establishing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime in India with effect from 1 July 2017.

questions.question: Under Section 8(1) of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, which of the following categories of information is exempt from public disclosure?

options.a: Information disclosure of which would prejudicially affect the sovereignty and security of India
options.b: Information older than five years concerning municipal taxes
options.c: Information relating to rural development expenditure
options.d: Minutes of public university senate meetings

questions.explanation: Section 8(1)(a) explicitly exempts information whose disclosure would prejudicially affect the sovereignty and integrity of India, state security, strategy, scientific or economic interests.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, is correct?

options.a: It can be conferred upon foreign citizens as well as Indian citizens
options.b: It must be awarded every calendar year without exception
options.c: It carries a cash prize of fifty lakh rupees
options.d: It can be awarded to a maximum of ten individuals in a single year

questions.explanation: There is no formal requirement that the recipient must be an Indian citizen. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987) and Nelson Mandela (1990) received the Bharat Ratna.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions publishes the annual 'World Economic Outlook' (WEO) report?
questions.explanation: The World Economic Outlook is a survey published biannually by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) analyzing global economic trends and GDP growth forecasts.

questions.question: Which one of the following indices is currently used as the headline measure of inflation by the Reserve Bank of India for monetary policy targeting?
questions.explanation: Following the recommendations of the Urjit Patel Committee in 2014, the RBI officially adopted Consumer Price Index - Combined (CPI-C, base year 2012) for inflation targeting (4% +/- 2%).

questions.question: According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) noise standards in India, what is the permissible ambient noise level in a residential area during daytime?
questions.explanation: CPCB noise limits for residential zones are 55 dB(A) Leq during daytime (6 AM to 10 PM) and 45 dB(A) Leq during nighttime.

questions.question: In which North African country did the popular pro-democracy uprisings known as the 'Arab Spring' originate in December 2010?
questions.explanation: The Arab Spring started in Tunisia in December 2010 following the self-immolation of Mohamed Bouazizi, leading to the Jasmine Revolution and spreading across North Africa and the Middle East.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the National Wildlife Action Plan (NWAP) of India for 2017-2031:

2. The NWAP is unique as this is the first time India has recognized the concerns relating to climate change impact on wildlife.
3. The NWAP has ten components.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The NWAP 2017-2031 is India's 3rd National Wildlife Action Plan. It is notable for integrating climate change impacts into wildlife planning for the first time. It has 17 priority themes and 103 conservation actions.

questions.explanation: INS Vikrant (formerly HMS Hercules) was India's first aircraft carrier, commissioned in 1961. Her Sea Hawk aircraft played a heroic role during the 1971 Liberation War in East Pakistan.

questions.question: Which of the following sprinter won three gold medals and set world records in 100m, 200m, and 4x100m relay at the 2008 Beijing Olympics?

questions.question: Which one of the following was historically designated as the longest National Highway in India connecting Varanasi to Kanyakumari?
questions.explanation: Under the old national highway numbering system, NH 7 (2,369 km) connecting Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu was the longest highway in India (now part of NH 44).

questions.question: Which one of the following is the correct order of the layers of the Earth's atmosphere starting from the surface upwards?
questions.explanation: From ground to space: Troposphere (0-12 km), Stratosphere (12-50 km, contains ozone layer), Mesosphere (50-85 km), Thermosphere (85-600 km), and Exosphere.

questions.question: Which one of the following Southeast Asian countries shares a land border with both India and China and acts as a gateway for India's Act East Policy?
questions.explanation: Myanmar borders four northeast Indian states (Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram) and also shares borders with China, Laos, Thailand, and Bangladesh.

questions.explanation: Rafael Nadal won his maiden Wimbledon title in 2008 in a historic match widely considered one of the greatest tennis finals in history.

questions.question: Who among the following was known as the 'Iron Man of India' and served as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India?
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel orchestrated the integration of over 560 princely states into the Indian Union, earning the title 'Iron Man of India' and 'Bismarck of India'.

questions.question:
According to the Constitution (Fifty-Second Amendment) Act 1985 as amended in 2003, a legislator attracts disqualification under the Tenth Schedule if:
1. He voluntarily gives up the membership of the party on whose ticket he was elected.
2. He votes or abstains from voting contrary to any direction issued by his political party.
3. As a result of split, less than one-third of the members formed a new group or party in the house.
4. A member who has been elected as an independent member joins any political party.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.explanation: Under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law), a member is disqualified if they voluntarily give up party membership, vote contrary to party whip without prior permission, or if an independent member joins any political party. The 91st Amendment (2003) deleted the exemption for 1/3rd split, requiring at least 2/3rd for merger.

questions.question: In democratic political theory and constitutional design, why is power sharing considered desirable in diverse societies?

options.a: It reduces the possibility of conflict and alienation between social groups
options.b: It eliminates the need for holding regular elections
options.c: It concentrates decision-making power in the executive branch
options.d: It allows the majority community to impose its will without compromise

questions.explanation: Power sharing accommodates social diversity, prevents majoritarian domination, and fosters political stability by giving all communities a stake in governance.

questions.question: The Second Backward Classes Commission, popularly known as the Mandal Commission, submitted its report recommending 27% reservations for OBCs in public employment in:
questions.explanation: Appointed in 1979 by the Morarji Desai government under B.P. Mandal, the Commission submitted its report in December 1980. It was implemented in 1990 under Prime Minister V.P. Singh.

questions.question: What does the author mean by "authen- tic' civil society" ?

options.a: people who have lost faith in parliamentary system
options.b: Citizens who are not corrupt but do not vote
options.c: Citizens who passionately advocate the cleansing of institutional mal- practices and 'societal injustices through non parliamentary methods
options.d: Activists who want moral accounta- bility and judicial redress of all wrong doings in society

questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Defence, Military & Current Affairs).

questions.question: Which of the following Writs literally means 'We Command' and is issued to enforce the performance of a mandatory public duty?
questions.explanation: Mandamus literally translates to 'We Command'. It is an order issued by the Supreme Court (Art 32) or High Court (Art 226) to any public authority or inferior tribunal commanding them to perform an obligatory public duty.

questions.question: Which one among the following pairs of level of government and legislative power is not correctly matched ?

questions.question: Which one of the following Constitutional Amendments deleted the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 abolished the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right (Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31) and made it a constitutional/legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.

questions.question: The Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament is summoned by the President under Article

options.a: The Vice-President of India (Chairman of Rajya Sabha)
options.d: The Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs

questions.explanation: The Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Article 118(4)). In the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker presides; in their absence, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides.

questions.question: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India in 1946.
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission sent by Clement Attlee in March 1946 consisted of three British cabinet ministers: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander. Lord Wavell was the Viceroy of India, not a Mission member.

questions.question: Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, and Shrieking Sixties are terms applied to strong westerly winds found
questions.explanation: In the Southern Hemisphere between 40° and 60°S latitude, the lack of landmasses allows the prevailing westerlies to blow with extreme unobstructed velocity, termed Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, and Shrieking Sixties.

questions.question: Which one of the following gases is responsible for the effervescence observed when baking soda is added to vinegar?
questions.explanation: When sodium bicarbonate (baking soda, NaHCO3) reacts with acetic acid (vinegar, CH3COOH), sodium acetate, water, and carbon dioxide (CO2) gas are produced. The rapid release of CO2 produces vigorous effervescence.

questions.question: Which one of the following major rivers of India flows westward and empties into the Arabian Sea rather than the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapti rivers flow westward through tectonic rift valleys and empty into the Arabian Sea via the Gulf of Khambhat. Mahanadi, Godavari, and Cauvery flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: An object has a mass of 6 kg on the surface of the Earth. When taken to the Moon (where acceleration due to gravity is 1/6th that of Earth), its mass will be:
questions.explanation: Mass is an intrinsic property representing the amount of matter in a body and remains constant everywhere (6 kg). Only the weight (W = mg) decreases to 1/6th on the Moon.

questions.question: For the same rise in temperature, which of the three states of matter undergoes the greatest volumetric thermal expansion?
questions.explanation: Gases exhibit the highest coefficient of thermal expansion because intermolecular forces are minimal, allowing particles to move far apart when heated.

questions.question: In the human digestive system, the opening of the stomach into the small intestine (duodenum) is regulated by the:
questions.explanation: The pyloric sphincter is a band of smooth muscle at the junction between the pylorus of the stomach and the duodenum of the small intestine that controls the flow of chyme.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the United Nations based at The Hague, is composed of how many judges elected for a nine-year term?
questions.explanation: The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected by the UN General Assembly and Security Council for 9-year terms. Five judges are elected every three years.

questions.question: The human body's primary sensory organ responsible for maintaining balance, posture, and equilibrium is located in the:
questions.explanation: The vestibular apparatus in the inner ear, consisting of the three semicircular canals, utricle, and saccule, detects head motion and gravity to maintain balance and equilibrium.

questions.question: What is a 'Green Data Centre'?

options.a: A data centre created by environmentalists to keep records of clean production technology
options.b: A repository for storage and management of data where mechanical, electrical, and computer systems are optimized for maximum energy efficiency and minimal environmental footprint
options.c: A data centre for green buildings optimizing power consumption using solar energy
options.d: A repository providing information about small industries adopting energy efficiency measures

questions.explanation: A green data centre is an enterprise storage repository where lighting, electrical, cooling, and compute systems are engineered to achieve maximum power usage effectiveness (PUE) and minimal carbon emissions.

questions.question: What is the primary chemical compound that constitutes natural pearls and sea shells?
questions.explanation: Pearls and mollusk shells consist primarily of calcium carbonate (CaCO3, mostly in the form of aragonite crystals) deposited in concentric layers held together by the organic protein conchiolin.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements relating to the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) is/are correct?
1. It was founded to maintain independence from rival Cold War power blocs.
2. Military alliances formed a core component of NAM.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: NAM originated at the 1955 Bandung Conference and 1961 Belgrade Summit. Statement 2 is incorrect: NAM was explicitly non-military and rejected joining Cold War military alliances like NATO or the Warsaw Pact.

questions.question: Which of the following infectious diseases is caused by a protozoan parasite and transmitted by the bite of the sandfly?
questions.explanation: Kala-azar (Visceral leishmaniasis) is caused by the protozoan parasite Leishmania donovani and transmitted to humans by the bite of infected female phlebotomine sandflies.

questions.question: Which one among the following natural or artificial processes produces light through a chemical reaction (chemiluminescence)?
questions.explanation: Fireflies produce light through bioluminescence, a form of chemiluminescence where the pigment luciferin is oxidized in the presence of the enzyme luciferase and ATP without producing heat.

questions.question: Which one of the following elements is essential for the formation of chlorophyll in green plants?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Solution: Assessed under General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology) according to UPSC CDS standards.

questions.question: Which one of the following human diseases is caused by a protozoan parasite and NOT by bacteria or viruses?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium (transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito). Tetanus is bacterial; Measles and Mumps are viral diseases.

questions.question: Which one of the following chemical compounds is widely used as a mordant in the textile dyeing and leather tanning industries?
questions.explanation: Potash alum (potassium aluminum sulfate) acts as a mordant by providing aluminum ions that bind natural dyes to textile fibers, fixing colors permanently.

questions.question: Which one of the following viral diseases is transmitted to humans by the bite of the female Aedes aegypti mosquito?
questions.explanation: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes transmit Dengue, Chikungunya, Zika, and Yellow fever. Malaria is spread by Anopheles, Kala-azar by sandflies, and sleeping sickness by tsetse flies.

questions.question: Which one of the following parameters will remain constant during the fall ?
questions.explanation: Official UPSC CDS Rationale: Tested in CDS General Knowledge (Defence, Military & Current Affairs).

questions.question: Which one of the following is responsible for the stimulating effect of tea?
questions.explanation: The stimulating effect of tea is primarily due to the purine alkaloid caffeine (also known as theine), which acts as a central nervous system stimulant.

questions.question: Fiscal Deficit in the Union Budget of India is defined as:

options.a: Total Expenditure minus Total Receipts (excluding borrowings)
options.c: Total Expenditure minus Tax Revenue only
options.d: Monetary deficit financed by RBI loans

questions.explanation: Fiscal Deficit = Total Budget Expenditure - Total Receipts excluding borrowings. It represents the total borrowing requirements of the government from all sources.

questions.question: Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), also known as 'paper gold', are supplementary foreign exchange reserve assets created by:
questions.explanation: SDRs were created by the IMF in 1969 to supplement member countries' official reserves. The SDR basket includes the US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi, Japanese Yen, and British Pound.

questions.question: The Phillips Curve in macroeconomic theory illustrates an inverse relationship between:

options.a: Rate of inflation and rate of unemployment
options.c: Tax rates and total tax revenue collection
options.d: Income level and demand for inferior goods

questions.explanation: The Phillips Curve, formulated by A.W. Phillips in 1958, shows an empirical inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.

questions.question: The difference between total revenue expenditure and total revenue receipts of the government in a financial year is called:
questions.explanation: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts. It signifies that the government is borrowing to finance its day-to-day administrative consumption expenditure.

questions.question: Which of the following macroeconomic policy measures is typically adopted by monetary and fiscal authorities to curb high inflation in an economy?

options.a: Raising the repo rate and reducing public expenditure
options.b: Lowering statutory reserve ratios (CRR and SLR)
options.d: Expanding public subsidies and tax holidays

questions.explanation: To tame inflation (contractionary policy), central banks hike interest rates (repo rate) to tighten liquidity and credit, while the government reduces public spending and fiscal deficits.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included while calculating the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of India?

options.a: Transfer payments (such as old-age pensions and scholarships)

questions.explanation: Transfer payments are unilateral payments made without any corresponding exchange of goods or services in return, and are therefore excluded from GDP calculations.

questions.question: Which one of the following public sector banks in India historically had an emblem featuring a dog with the motto 'Faithful, Friendly' before its merger with Canara Bank?
questions.explanation: Syndicate Bank, established in 1925 in Manipal, Karnataka, was famously known for its symbol of a faithful dog and the tagline 'Faithful, Friendly'. It was amalgamated into Canara Bank in 2020.

questions.question: According to the official Census of India, which one among the following Indian States has consistently recorded the highest female literacy rate?
questions.explanation: Kerala ranks highest in overall literacy and female literacy in India (over 92% female literacy).

Which of the following statements about the commonly used automobile battery are true?
1. It is usually a lead-acid battery.
2. It has six cells with a potential of 2 Volt each.

4. Its cells work as electrolytic cells while recharging.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.explanation: A standard 12V car battery consists of six 2V lead-acid cells connected in series. When delivering current it operates as a galvanic cell (chemical to electrical); when being recharged by the alternator it operates as an electrolytic cell.

questions.question: Which one of the following is responsible for the stimulating effect of tea?

questions.question: Primary Deficit in public finance is mathematically computed by deducting which one of the following from the Fiscal Deficit?
questions.explanation: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments. It indicates government borrowing requirements strictly to finance ongoing fiscal policies excluding past debt obligations.

questions.question: The Lorenz Curve in economics is a graphical representation used to measure:

options.a: Income inequality and wealth distribution in a population
options.c: Relationship between tax rate and tax revenue
options.d: Consumer price index variation over time

questions.explanation: The Lorenz Curve plots cumulative percentage of population against cumulative percentage of income earned. The Gini Coefficient is derived directly from the area between the line of equality and the Lorenz Curve.

questions.question: The concept of 'Gross National Happiness' (GNH) as a measure of national development progress was first introduced by which country?
questions.explanation: Gross National Happiness (GNH) was instituted in 1972 by Jigme Singye Wangchuck, the 4th King of Bhutan, measuring social development and environmental conservation alongside economics.

questions.question: What was the target deadline year set by the United Nations for achieving the eight Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) adopted in the year 2000?
questions.explanation: The Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) established eight anti-poverty and development goals with measurable targets to be achieved by the year 2015, succeeded by the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

questions.question: Which of the following rates is known as the key policy interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends short-term liquidity to commercial banks against government securities?

questions.question: For which one of the following landmark judgments of the Supreme Court of India is the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) famous?

options.c: Formulation of the creamy layer principle in reservations
options.d: Striking down the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)

questions.question: The historic 'Panchsheel' (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was formally enunciated in 1954 in an agreement between India and which country?

questions.question: What is a 'Concordat' in international diplomacy and legal history?

questions.question: Which one among the following is the primary constitutional function of the Pro-Tem Speaker of the Lok Sabha?

options.b: Preside over the joint sitting of Parliament in the absence of the Speaker
options.c: Check whether election certificates of all members are authentic
options.d: Decide on the disqualification of members under the Tenth Schedule

questions.explanation: The Pro-Tem Speaker is appointed by the President (typically the senior-most member) to preside over the initial sitting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha, administer oath/affirmation to new MPs, and conduct the election of the permanent Speaker.

questions.question: Which one among the following statements regarding the erstwhile Planning Commission of India is NOT correct?

questions.question: Which one of the following Fundamental Rights under the Constitution of India is also available to non-citizens (foreigners)?

questions.question: Fiscal Deficit in the Union Budget of India is defined as:

options.c: Total Expenditure minus Tax Revenue only

questions.explanation: Fiscal Deficit = Total Budget Expenditure - Total Receipts excluding borrowings. It represents the total borrowing requirements of the government from all sources.

questions.question: The difference between total revenue expenditure and total revenue receipts of the government in a financial year is called:

questions.question: Which of the following macroeconomic policy measures is typically adopted by monetary and fiscal authorities to curb high inflation in an economy?

options.d: Expanding public subsidies and tax holidays

questions.explanation: To tame inflation (contractionary policy), central banks hike interest rates (repo rate) to tighten liquidity and credit, while the government reduces public spending and fiscal deficits.

questions.question: Which one of the following Indian states has the longest coastline among all peninsular states of mainland India?

questions.question: Which one of the following major rivers of India flows westward and empties into the Arabian Sea rather than the Bay of Bengal?

questions.question: An object has a mass of 6 kg on the surface of the Earth. When taken to the Moon (where acceleration due to gravity is 1/6th that of Earth), its mass will be:

questions.question: For the same rise in temperature, which of the three states of matter undergoes the greatest volumetric thermal expansion?

questions.question: In the human digestive system, the opening of the stomach into the small intestine (duodenum) is regulated by the:

questions.question: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the United Nations based at The Hague, is composed of how many judges elected for a nine-year term?
questions.explanation: The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected by the UN General Assembly and Security Council for 9-year terms. Five judges are elected every three years.

questions.question: The human body's primary sensory organ responsible for maintaining balance, posture, and equilibrium is located in the:
questions.explanation: The vestibular apparatus in the inner ear, consisting of the three semicircular canals, utricle, and saccule, detects head motion and gravity to maintain balance and equilibrium.

questions.explanation: The family is the primary agency of socialization where a child first acquires language, behavioral norms, emotional attachments, and cultural values.

questions.question: The historic 'Panchsheel' (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was formally enunciated in 1954 in an agreement between India and which country?

questions.question: What is a 'Concordat' in international diplomacy and legal history?

questions.question: Which one among the following is the primary constitutional function of the Pro-Tem Speaker of the Lok Sabha?

questions.explanation: The Pro-Tem Speaker is appointed by the President (typically the senior-most member) to preside over the initial sitting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha, administer oath/affirmation to new MPs, and conduct the election of the permanent Speaker.

questions.question: Which one among the following statements regarding the erstwhile Planning Commission of India is NOT correct?

options.b: It was a statutory body established under an Act of the Parliament
